meta.title: How a Slack message becomes committed work
meta.subtitle: The dispatch bridge end to end, including the two ways it stops

segments.label: Auto-trigger — Warden decides on its own

messages.label: the brief on stdin, never as an argument
messages.note: A brief is data. It never becomes an argv element, so nothing in it can be read as a flag.

messages.label: Approve / Deny, and stop here
messages.note: Only the implement tier is gated. Investigate and author run straight through. No recursion, repo resolves, not denied, budget left.

messages.label: Approve
messages.note: The signature covers the brief and the context bytes. Swap either after signing and the replay is refused.

messages.label: submit the job, and record the Slack thread it came from
messages.note: Verify the signature, then spend it once.

messages.label: cut a worktree: read-only, or writable for implement
pick the model and the credential from the routing table
messages.note: Cheap mechanical work runs on a gateway model. Judgment runs on Claude, and falls back to the metered key when the subscription quota is high.

messages.label: one verdict, or a timeout that is also a verdict
messages.note: Read, reason, and for implement, write.

messages.label: the verdict, in the same reply
or it took longer than the turn could wait
the verdict, into the original thread
messages.note: Three misses and it is marked lost, not retried forever.

messages.label: decides: --auto-from-item, no human gate
messages.note: The triage loop dispatches on its own; the Ask and Gate segments above never run for this path.

messages.label: submit the job, same policy and budget checks
the verdict, posted to the digest
